# Alpaca

**Summary**: An instruction-following language model created by fine-tuning the LLaMA model on 52K instruction-output pairs generated by OpenAI's text-davinci-003.
**Source Context**: Taori et al., "Stanford Alpaca: An instruction-following LLaMA model" (2023).

---

## Development and Methodology
Alpaca is a product of [[concepts/instruction-tuning.md]]. The authors used the Self-Instruct methodology, where a powerful "teacher" model (text-davinci-003) is prompted to generate a diverse set of instruction-output pairs. The smaller, open-source LLaMA model was then fine-tuned on this synthesized dataset [Source: [158]].

This approach demonstrated that a relatively small (7B parameter) model could exhibit compelling instruction-following behavior after targeted fine-tuning, making such capabilities more accessible.

## Impact and Legacy
Alpaca sparked significant activity in the open-source LLM community. It showed that high-quality instruction-tuning data could be generated semi-automatically. It was quickly followed by other instruction-tuned variants like Vicuna, which used user-shared conversations from ChatGPT for fine-tuning, and WizardLM, which used more complex instruction evolution [Source: [159], [163]].
